answer: Trust propagates from independently anchored identities through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition weights normalized by vertex degree. A Sybil cluster can become a garden of hollow, mutually endorsing accounts, yet a sparse external cut gives it low conductance: few walks enter from honest seeds. With capped path influence, min-cut bounds thus constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, preventing internal endorsements from multiplying it without limit.
